raw_response:
I farm the same 10.7 mu in wheat-maize rotation, so I will put all 10.7 mu into wheat first, then all 10.7 mu into maize after wheat harvest. I do not like changing too much at once. What worked last year, I will keep, then adjust a little by how the crop looked and what people around me did. With well water in hand, I am not as scared of dry spells, so I will keep fertilizer and water steady to protect yield. I only finished primary school, but after farming 30 years I do watch the balance a bit. Wheat needs a solid base fertilizer and at least a few waterings. Maize grows fast after it gets going, so I will not let it run short of nitrogen. Fertilizer costs money, that is true, but losing yield costs more, so I would rather put a bit extra than come up short. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because that is what most people around me use now and I have seen it pay. For wheat I will plough after maize, put on base fertilizer, irrigate at sowing if the soil is dry, then water again at jointing and filling. For maize I will mostly use rotary tillage after wheat harvest, sow quickly, put most fertilizer under or beside the row, then topdress once when it is knee-high to waist-high, with two irrigations if rain is not enough. Pesticide I will not spray blindly, but I will plan a couple of times on each crop because on my side if I wait too long, it is easy to lose more than the spray costs.
